title: The roof before the last day
question: Tomorrow is the last day anything new can be promoted. What did rounds 4 to 6 teach us about how we work, and what should round 7 (Tue 3 Nov) chase?
serves: Creativity & Presentation ('a compelling, well-organized narrative in an authentic team voice') and the IPS instruction 'Clearly explain your team's investment strategy and the reasoning behind it'; Book 11 items 6 and 7 (every sentence plain; the over-compression fingerprint); Commandment IV
essence: We argued about what cutting one sentence taught us, and the slip we blamed on the people who cut it was made later, by my own group.
We decided that whoever cuts a sentence first says what leaned on it and what takes over.
Tomorrow the IPS gets plainer words wherever a stranger would guess, and "her promise" stays only if a stranger with your Trading Notes open reads it as the building money.
decided: 2-1 (Jun for Nora's strangers rule): LS-15, 'Before a room cuts or moves a line, it searches the register for that line, reads out every job it does and every HOLD that leaned on it, and names the line that carries each one afterwards.'

3-0: LS-10 raised to 2, counted by date like LS-06 (bent Thu 29 Oct, broken Mon 2 Nov); on Tuesday P8 gets two beats, the Window and the Writing Room. LS-14 raised to 1; LS-06 and LS-13 marked ruled (the vote gate)
3-0: round 7 asks Q15, 'Which words in D plus the cure would the weakest stranger have to guess, and what do people who explain money for a living put first?'; lens 19, the child's question

3-0: scouts are round 5's fields swapped: Amara near (capital-protected notes; line 71), Kai adjacent (weather forecasts; lines 89-90), Jun far (medicine leaflets and their pass mark; line 34); no scout brings back a sentence to paste
3-0: Felix builds, Tess hunts flaws, Nora judges cold (pass mark first, strangers counted, the weakest reader decides)

3-0: 'No fourth flip' stands for the last line and F20 closes with D; F21's HOLD is void on D, the Window reads it out at 08:40 and a TNA-open stranger settles 'her promise' at 16:20; the 18:20 Courtroom records it, no vote
seeds: The case says 'promise' only of the 2031 range and calls the cheques 'the operating commitment'; the pitch calls the cheques 'a promise'. Which word should the pitch use, and does the IPS change with it? (Window and Writing Room, Tue 3 Nov)

A medicine leaflet must pass a readers' test on every question, not on average (Norway's medicines agency, 90% find and 90% of those understand). Is there a version of that pass mark a three-reader panel can honestly use? (Nora's judge sheet)
